note: Original intents restated for the current architecture and grouped into capabilities (2026-11-22). Planner material; executors never read it.

capabilities.name: Install warns when a spec document could not be converted
capabilities.user_story: A user whose project sets spec_format=xml installs a package whose PROP-001.md is malformed. `vibe install` now prints `warning: org.acme/pkg@1.2.0: vibevm/vibespecs/PROP-001.md kept as Markdown (conversion failed: <parse error>)`, and `vibe install --json` carries a `conversion_fallbacks` array naming package, file, kept format and reason. With `--strict-conversion` the same install refuses before any slot, lock or boot lane is published, naming the file.
capabilities.todays_form: Extends the legacy (non-declared) materialisation path only: crates/vibe-workspace/src/vibedeps/derived.rs transform_file (lines ~348-372, today `Err(_) => return Ok(None)` for unreadable text and for parse failure) and crates/vibe-workspace/src/vibedeps/derived/materialise.rs (which then records SlotFileDisposition::Copied). The reason is carried out in MaterialiseReport (crates/vibe-workspace/src/vibedeps/slot_diff/report.rs) and into the install outcome (crates/vibe-workspace/src/install/model.rs, next to `integrity_warnings`), emitted like integrity warnings in crates/vibe-install/src/apply.rs:475 and rendered in crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/install/report.rs. The declared-source path (derived/declared.rs) already refuses fatally and is not changed. Not rebuilt: no proof slice, no new slot-record schema, no closure-diff changes.
rough_steps: transform_file returns a typed fallback (enum ConversionFallback { Unreadable(String), Unparseable(String) }) instead of a bare Ok(None) when an opposite-format spec document is not converted; non-opposite files keep returning None
materialise_with_spec_format_report collects fallbacks into MaterialiseReport.conversion_fallbacks; the public footprint wrapper ignores them

InstallOutcome gains conversion_fallbacks: Vec<String>-like typed rows; apply.rs emits one warn line per row; install/update/reinstall human output prints them under a 'warnings' heading; --json adds the array
Add --strict-conversion to install, update and reinstall; when set, any fallback is a refusal raised before publication (inside the existing rollback boundary)
Fixture test: malformed .md under spec_format=xml -> warning in human and JSON output, slot still installed; with --strict-conversion -> nonzero exit, no lock/slot change
capabilities.acceptance: Fixture package with a malformed .md, consumer spec_format=xml: `vibe install --json` exits 0 and its JSON has conversion_fallbacks[0].file == the .md path and kept_format == "markdown"; human output contains 'kept as Markdown'. `vibe install --strict-conversion` exits nonzero, vibe.lock and vibedeps unchanged. Same package with valid .md: no fallbacks field entries.
design_decisions: Default stays non-fatal (derived.rs:86 docstring preserves availability); strictness is opt-in
Strict switch is a CLI flag `--strict-conversion` on install/update/reinstall, not a vibe.toml key in this release; a manifest key can follow if asked
JSON field name `conversion_fallbacks`, rows {package, version, file, kept_format ("markdown"|"xml"), reason}
Human line format: `warning: <group/name>@<version>: <file> kept as <Markdown|XML> (conversion failed: <reason>)`
Only opposite-format spec documents (is_spec_document + opposite) are reported; ordinary copied files are never warnings
Overlay-targeted failures keep their existing hard error
Slot record schema unchanged: disposition Copied already records the outcome
capabilities.risks: Noise if many legacy packages contain unparseable Markdown; mitigated by one line per file and no repeat for skipped (already-present) slots. Related conversion-fidelity issue BACKLOG B-205 is separate and not fixed here.

capabilities.name: Read one spec section by its spec:// address
capabilities.user_story: An agent or user sees `spec://org.vibevm.core/vibevm/common/PROP-000#commits` in boot text and runs `vibe show section spec://org.vibevm.core/vibevm/common/PROP-000#commits`; it prints that section's text from the version the lock selects, preceded by a one-line origin header (package@version, slot-relative file, converted/copied/authored, sha256). `--json` returns the same as fields; an MCP tool `read_spec` returns the same JSON. A bad address, an uninstalled package, a pin that does not match the lock or a missing anchor gives a typed refusal naming the cause, not a guess.
capabilities.todays_form: A thin read over the existing resolver: vibe_spec::SpecAddress::parse (crates/vibe-spec/src/address.rs), FileResolver::with_selected_world (crates/vibe-spec/src/resolver.rs:273) and FsSectionSource::section_text / expand_embeds (crates/vibe-spec/src/embed.rs), the same composition already used by crates/vibe-lifecycle/src/agent/resolver.rs:104, crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/facts/selected.rs:147 and show/effective/read.rs:313. One shared function lives in vibe-workspace (which both vibe-cli and vibe-mcp already depend on) and builds the selected world the way facts/selected.rs does. Origin comes from the existing slot record (.vibe-slot.toml rows: source, sha256, SlotFileDisposition) via vibedeps::read_derived_manifest / slot_record. CLI adapter: new ShowSubcommand::Section in crates/vibe-cli/src/cli/inspect.rs + crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/show/section.rs. MCP adapter: crates/vibe-mcp/src/tools/read_spec.rs beside read_doc. Replaces the original 'generated source-query service, pagination cursors, proof strengths, parity report': none of that is built; parity is a test asserting CLI --json and MCP output are equal.
capabilities.product_question: Add the new public surface `vibe show section` + MCP `read_spec` now, rather than waiting for the M-16/M-17 machine-surface work?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Yes: agents already meet spec:// links in boot and today guess vibedeps paths; the surface is two thin adapters over one existing resolver, so M-16/M-17 can adopt it rather than conflict with it.
rough_steps: vibe-workspace: `spec_section::read(project_root, &SpecAddress, ReadOptions{expand_embeds}) -> Result<SectionRead, SectionRefusal>` building the selected world from vibe.lock like facts/selected.rs, reading through FsSectionSource
Attach origin: package, selected version, slot-relative file, disposition from the slot record (authored for the self coordinate), sha256 of the bytes actually read
`vibe show section <ADDRESS> [--path DIR] [--expand-embeds] [--json]` with plain output = header line + text
MCP tool `read_spec` {address, expand_embeds?} returning the same JSON object
Tests: own-project section, installed dependency section, converted XML slot, missing anchor, unknown package, version pin mismatch, CLI/MCP JSON equality
capabilities.acceptance: `vibe show section spec://org.vibevm.core/vibevm/common/PROP-000#commits` in this repo prints the commits section; `--json` has ok=true, package, version, file, disposition, sha256, text. `vibe show section spec://no.such/pkg/X#a` exits nonzero with refusal kind `not-installed`. MCP tools/list includes read_spec and calling it returns byte-identical JSON to the CLI --json output.
design_decisions: Subcommand name `vibe show section` (show already hosts read-only inspectors such as source-path, effective)
MCP tool name `read_spec` (parallel to read_doc; read_doc stays documentation-only)
Address without #anchor returns the whole document
Default does NOT expand #embed; `--expand-embeds` opts in (agents usually want the literal section with its links)
JSON fields: ok, command:"show section", address, package, version, file, format ("xml"|"markdown"), disposition ("authored"|"converted"|"copied"), sha256, text
Refusal kinds (kebab-case `kind` field + existing ResolveError message): invalid-address, not-installed, version-mismatch, anchor-not-found, outside-package, unreadable-source
Version comes only from the lock-selected world; a pinned @version that differs from the lock is refused, never fetched
Ordinary Markdown exports and raw resources: return bytes verbatim when UTF-8; a non-UTF-8 resource is refused with a hint to `vibe show source-path`
No pagination, no cursors, no proof-strength labels; sha256 is of the exact buffer returned
capabilities.risks: Selected-world construction is currently private to CLI call sites; lifting it into vibe-workspace must not fork its logic (move, don't copy). Overlap with M-16/M-17 naming if those later redefine show verbs.

capabilities.name: Preview the boot change before installing
capabilities.user_story: Before adding a package, a user runs `vibe install org.acme/big-pack --plan-only --boot-delta` and sees, under the closure plan, `boot: vibevm/vibespecs/boot/STATIC.xml 41.2 KB -> 58.9 KB (+17.7 KB)` for each watched lane, computed from the full candidate closure (shared dependencies counted once). Nothing in the project changes. The same works for `vibe update --plan-only --boot-delta` and for removing a direct dependency.
capabilities.todays_form: Extends the existing no-publication preview: crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/install/preview.rs (already resolves into an owned tempdir scratch) and reuses closure_diff.rs (ClosureDiff.lane_bytes, lane_sizes, watched_lanes) for rendering. The candidate boot is computed by copying the project's authored inputs into a scratch project, materialising the candidate closure there with the existing install path (vibe-workspace install + install/bootgen), then sampling lane_sizes in scratch vs. the real root. Fetch uses the existing package-source acquisition into a scratch storage root, exactly as personal.rs:173 preview_scratch does. Replaces the original hypothetical-world capture, effectful-preparation framework and scenario editor; reconfigure/feature what-if is not built.
capabilities.product_question: Is a pre-install boot-size delta worth having `--plan-only --boot-delta` download package content (an effect plan-only otherwise avoids)?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Yes, behind the explicit opt-in flag: 'how much will this add to my agent's boot' is answered today only after install, and the fetch goes to a throwaway scratch reusing existing acquisition code.
rough_steps: `--boot-delta` flag on install (requires --plan-only) and on update; refused with --global
Scratch project: copy vibe.toml/vibe.lock/authored vibespecs into a tempdir; storage root = scratch (personal.rs precedent); run the normal install apply against the scratch root
Sample closure_diff::lane_sizes(real root) and lane_sizes(scratch root), produce ClosureDiff.lane_bytes, render with closure_diff::render
Removal case: `vibe uninstall <pkg> --plan-only --boot-delta` for project dependencies uses the same scratch apply (no fetch needed)
JSON: InstallPlan output gains `boot_delta: [{lane, before, after}]`; tests on fixture registries including a shared-dependency case proving non-additivity
capabilities.acceptance: Fixture: project with A installed, B shares A's dependency. `vibe install B --plan-only --boot-delta --json` has boot_delta rows whose after-before equals the delta seen after a real `vibe install B`; project tree byte-identical before/after the preview (git status clean). Without --boot-delta, plan-only output and effects unchanged.
design_decisions: Flag name `--boot-delta`, valid only with `--plan-only` (install, update, project uninstall)
Lanes watched = closure_diff::watched_lanes(); same units and rendering as the post-apply closure diff
Fetch target is a per-run tempdir storage root, deleted on exit; offline mode uses only the cache and reports unavailable packages as an error naming them
Never sum per-package sizes; always compare two full builds
JSON field `boot_delta` on the existing wire InstallPlan (add optional field via vibe-wire generated schema)
Lifecycle hooks / post-install tasks are NOT run in the scratch apply
capabilities.risks: Scratch apply must not touch user-global state (registry cache writes, settings, lifecycle records); needs a review of every effect the install path performs. Cost: a full materialise per preview.

capabilities.name: Exact boot sizes and honest unreadable lanes in vibe tree
capabilities.user_story: `vibe tree` and `vibe tree --json` report each STATIC contribution's size as the exact byte count of its range in the lane file (CRLF and missing final newline counted correctly), and a lane that exists but cannot be read shows as `unreadable: <error>` instead of being silently treated as absent.
capabilities.todays_form: Fixes crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/tree/artifacts.rs:106 (bytes estimated as sum(line.len()+1)) to measure the actual byte span, and crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/tree/build.rs:524 read_opt (collapses NotFound and other IO errors into None) into a tri-state. No tokenizer, no quota, no qualified measurement reports.
rough_steps: Compute contribution bytes from line byte offsets of the raw lane text
read_opt -> enum LaneRead { Absent, Present(String), Unreadable(String) }; render Unreadable in plain/TUI/JSON
Tests: CRLF lane, no trailing newline, unreadable lane (permission-denied fixture on unix)
capabilities.acceptance: A CRLF STATIC lane fixture: sum of contribution bytes in `vibe tree --json` equals the bytes of those ranges in the file. A chmod 000 STATIC lane: JSON shows lane state "unreadable" with the error, not absent.
design_decisions: JSON: lane object gets `state: "present"|"absent"|"unreadable"` and `error` when unreadable; existing fields unchanged
Unreadable lane is a reported state, not a command failure (exit 0)
capabilities.risks: JSON consumers that assumed absent==None; additive field keeps compatibility.

capabilities.name: Install from deep Windows project roots, verified natively
capabilities.user_story: A Windows user whose project lives under a long corporate profile or worktree path runs `vibe install`; it either succeeds or fails with `path too long: <path> (<n> chars, limit <m>); move the project to a shorter root or enable long paths`, before any partial slot is published. The filesystem safety suite (symlink/alias/observation adversaries) is shown to pass on native Windows and macOS.
capabilities.todays_form: Runs the existing install path and the existing vibe-safefs adversary tests natively. Code changes only if the run fails: in crates/vibe-safefs Windows platform (transaction/platform/operations.rs, handle-relative NtCreateFile) or slot materialisation in crates/vibe-workspace/src/vibedeps. Separate from BACKLOG B-132 (registry clone path in vibe-registry git_backend). The excluded historical five-file candidate is not resurrected.
prerequisites: native Windows host
native macOS host (for the E.1 half)
rough_steps: Add an ignored-by-default integration test creating a >200-char project root with a deeply nested package and running install
Run it and the vibe-safefs adversary suite on native Windows and macOS; record results
If materialisation fails: fix the failing call or add a pre-publication path-length check with the diagnostic
Wire the test into the Windows CI/manual-test list
capabilities.acceptance: On native Windows, `vibe install` in a >200-char root with a deep package succeeds, or exits nonzero with a message containing 'path too long' and the length, with vibedeps/lock unchanged. vibe-safefs adversary tests green on native Windows and macOS (logs attached).
design_decisions: Diagnostic wording: `path too long: <path> (<n> characters; this host's limit is <m>)` plus the fix hint
Check happens before publication, inside the existing rollback boundary
Evidence recorded as a manual-test record, not fabricated from Linux runs
capabilities.risks: Needs real hosts; cannot be closed from Linux. May turn out to be a no-code verification.

capabilities.name: Inspect an authored change and its origin drift
capabilities.user_story: A user who keeps a change under `<spec_root>/changes/<id>/` runs `vibe change show <id>` (or `vibe change check` for every change) and sees: validation errors with the field to fix, the role documents, each origin package pin compared with what is installed now (unchanged / changed / missing / not installed), whether each cited origin address still resolves, the intent and work hashes, and the work graph. `--json` gives the same report to agents and CI, and `vibe change check` exits non-zero when a change is invalid.
capabilities.todays_form: A thin read-only CLI command, `vibe change`, built on the library that already landed in 940f93db: `vibe_core::manifest::change` (ChangeId, ChangeContext::for_node, CHANGES_DIR, plan_change_migration) and `vibe_requirements::change::{read_saved_change, ChangeIdentityAnalysis}`. The drift check (the review half of C.1) compares `ChangeOrigin.package`/`manifest_sha256` and each `ChangeOriginDocument.sha256` with the locked package and its materialised slot (`vibe_workspace::vibedeps::slot_record::read_slot_record` + `SlotFile.sha256`, address to file through `vibe_spec::resolver::resolve_file`). Coverage (C.2) is one bounded `vibe_requirements::RequirementsQuery` per cited address with `--address-prefix` semantics, and the report marks a cited address `incomplete` when that query is truncated. It replaces the planned 'complete same-snapshot fact universe' with this simpler check. Not built: a generated operation-descriptor layer (M-16), a second verdict engine, origin authentication, editor-overlay reads, or MCP parity in this step.
capabilities.product_question: Are authored changes (`changes/<id>/change.toml`, PROP-071) a supported product feature that users may create and keep?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Yes. The grammar and identities are already accepted as spec/done and have no consumer. A read-only command is cheap, cannot damage anything, and is the only way that work reaches a user.
rough_steps: Add `Command::Change(ChangeArgs)` with subcommands `check` and `show` (new crates/vibe-cli/src/cli/change.rs + crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/change/{mod,show}.rs), following the requirements.rs split pattern.
`vibe change show <id>`: read_saved_change + identity analysis, then render roles, origins, work DAG, and intent/work hashes, as text and as global `--json`.
Add origin drift: resolve each origin pin against vibe.lock and the slot record, and report per-pin and per-document status.
Add coverage: for each cited origin address, one RequirementsQuery reports present / missing / incomplete(truncated).
`vibe change check [<id>...]`: validate every change under the spec root, report the declarations a migration plan would rewrite, and set the exit code.
Add CLI integration tests over the formats/corpora/change-manifest/e1 fixtures plus a fixture project with an installed origin package.
capabilities.acceptance: `vibe change show <id> --json` on a fixture project returns the intent/work hashes that the library tests already assert. Changing one byte in the installed origin's cited file turns that document's status to `changed`. Pinning a version that is not locked shows `not-installed`. `vibe change check` exits 1 on an invalid change.toml and prints the ChangeError field. `vibe change --help` lists check/show. No file under the project changes (byte-compare the tree before and after).
design_decisions: Command: `vibe change check [ID...] [--path DIR]` and `vibe change show ID [--path DIR]`. Use the global `--json` and the `--path` convention that `vibe requirements` uses.
Changes directory: `<spec_root>/changes/<id>/`, with spec_root from the selected project's configured spec root, never from change.toml (ChangeContext::for_node already enforces this).

Meaning of the origin hashes (PROP-071 leaves it undefined): `manifest_sha256` = sha256 of the origin package's vibe.toml in its slot. Document `sha256` = sha256 of the slot file that contains the cited address, i.e. the SlotFile.sha256 row. Record this as a new PROP-071 unit.
Drift status enum, wire spelling: `unchanged | changed | missing-document | not-installed | version-differs`. Report the locked version next to the pinned one.
Coverage status per cited address: `present | missing | incomplete`. `incomplete` is used only when the bounded query reports truncated.

JSON report fields: `change_id, valid, errors[{kind,field,reason}], roles[{role,path,normative,input}], origins[{package,locked_version,manifest:{declared,actual,status},documents[{address,declared,actual,status,coverage}]}], intent_hash, work_hash, work[{id,predecessors,needs}], migration_available`.
Exit codes: 0 when everything is valid, even if drift exists (drift is information). exit_code::GENERAL when any change is invalid. USAGE for an unknown id.
Read-only: no sync, no install, no network. Origin data comes only from the materialised slot, never from a fetch.
capabilities.risks: The doc-hash semantics in PROP-071 are undecided, so pick them once and test them. An executor may pull in the full M-01 capture stack or build pagination for C.2. The word 'overlay' is overloaded: this command never touches PackageOverlay or the slot overlay_hash. With no real change.toml in the repo, fixture-only coverage can hide UX gaps.

capabilities.name: Start a change from a package feature and re-base it
capabilities.user_story: A user runs `vibe change new --from spec://org.acme/payments/FEAT-004#DELIVERY --title "EU payouts"`. vibe creates `changes/<id>/` with change.toml (the exact origin pin and hashes taken from the installed package) and starter intent.md / acceptance.md that quote the origin text, and never overwrites an existing directory. After an upgrade, `vibe change rebase <id>` shows how each cited origin document changed between the pinned and the installed version. With `--accept` it moves the pin and hashes to the new origin. The user's own documents are left as they are.
capabilities.todays_form: Write subcommands on the same `vibe change` command. Scaffolding uses vibe_safefs::Project no-overwrite owned publication (the directory is created only when absent). The M13 apply_plan is not used, because it refuses an absent target. The rebase rewrites only the `[[origins]]` rows through the existing format-preserving TOML editor (crates/vibe-core/src/toml_preserve.rs, the same machinery plan_change_migration uses), and the old/new document diff reuses a line diff. The LCS unified diff in crates/vibe-specdoc/src/convert.rs should move to a shared helper rather than be copied. A.1's 'two consumers refine independently' needs no fixture framework: every scaffold is project-owned, and one CLI test with two projects shows it. Not built: editor barriers (M-16), recovery stores, automatic merging into user documents.
prerequisites: Inspect an authored change and its origin drift
rough_steps: `vibe change new --from <spec-address> [--id ID] [--title T] [--slug S]`: resolve the address in an installed dependency, compute hashes the same way show does, generate `chg-<32 hex>`, and publish the directory without overwriting.
Seed intent.md with a provenance header and a quote of the cited unit, and acceptance.md with a template, both normative inputs. Add closure.md as non-normative.

`vibe change rebase <id>`: dry run by default. For each origin it prints the pinned→locked version and a per-document unified diff of the cited unit (old bytes from the registry cache at the pinned version; a 'base unavailable' notice when it cannot be read offline).
`vibe change rebase <id> --accept`: rewrite only the origins rows (pin + hashes), keeping comments and metadata, then print the new intent hash.
Add tests: refuse an existing destination, keep human comments in TOML on rebase, give two projects independent ids and intent hashes from one origin.
capabilities.acceptance: `vibe change new --from <addr>` followed by `vibe change show <id>` reports every origin `unchanged`. A second `new` with the same `--id` fails and the existing bytes stay identical. After the fixture dependency is upgraded, `vibe change rebase <id>` prints a diff and changes nothing. `--accept` makes `show` report `unchanged` again, and intent.md/acceptance.md stay byte-identical.
design_decisions: Generated ID: `chg-` + 32 lowercase hex from a random UUIDv4 (the form ChangeId::parse already accepts). `--id` allows the bootstrap form.
`--from` accepts only a `spec://group/name/document#fact` address of an installed dependency. Origin package spelling `<kind>:<group>/<name>@=<locked version>`, as in the corpus representative.toml.
File names: change.toml, intent.md, acceptance.md, closure.md (the roles in the corpus). The Markdown starters carry no front matter.
Rebase is a dry run unless `--accept` is given. It never edits role documents, and it refuses when change.toml fails validation.
When the old base cannot be read (offline, version gone), the rebase dry run shows the new text only and the status `base-unavailable`. `--accept` still works, because the user is choosing to accept.
Writes go only through vibe_safefs::Project. No partial directory is left behind: on a failure, report which files were written.
capabilities.risks: The registry-cache read of an older version may need network. Keep it explicit and allow it to fail. Moving the diff helper out of vibe-specdoc touches another crate, so keep it to one small shared function. Generated IDs must stay deterministic in tests, so inject the source of randomness.

capabilities.name: Make a tracked local copy of a dependency file or tree
capabilities.user_story: A user runs `vibe derive org.acme/style:templates/report/ --to local/report/`. vibe copies the installed files into the project and records the package, version, path and per-file base hashes. `vibe derive list` and `vibe derive show <name>` list the files the user changed. After `vibe update`, `vibe derive diff <name>` shows, per file, what upstream changed and what the user changed. `vibe derive rebase <name>` takes upstream changes for files the user did not touch, reports conflicts without overwriting, and moves the recorded base. `vibe derive remove <name>` drops the record and, if nothing was edited, the copy.
capabilities.todays_form: A new `vibe derive` command for what `[layers]` replace/supplement (crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/layers.rs) and `vibe registry vendor` do not cover: non-spec files and whole trees, with later upstream comparison. It reads base bytes and hashes from the materialised slot (`read_slot_record`, `SlotFile.sha256`, `verify_recorded_files` in crates/vibe-workspace/src/vibedeps/slot_record.rs). The authored record is a new `[[derived]]` array in vibe.toml, parsed next to `layers` in crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/document.rs and edited with toml_preserve. Old-base bytes for the three-way diff come from the registry cache at the recorded exact version. The five-family matrix (A.1) reduces to one rule: byte copy for every file, line diff for UTF-8 text, hash-only status for binary. D.1 becomes a `derived from <pkg>@<ver>:<path>` annotation in `vibe tree` source views. D.2's revocation becomes `vibe derive remove`. A copy is ordinary project content, so it is activated by the normal project install/deploy and needs no separate grant. Not built: an activation authority model, a universal operation service, skill hydration (prepare_declared_skill_projection publishes a cache and must not be reused), M-06 structural Markdown/XML handling.
capabilities.product_question: Do we want a tracked local copy of dependency files and trees in addition to `[layers]` overrides and `vibe registry vendor`?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Yes, narrowly. Layers only cover addressed spec units, and vendor mirrors whole packages with no edit tracking. Copying a template or skill tree and later seeing what upstream changed is a common need that nothing serves today.
rough_steps: Add the `[[derived]]` manifest section (name, from, path, to, base_sha256) to the vibe-core manifest, with parse and validation tests (portable relative paths, unique names, `to` inside the project, not under vibedeps).
`vibe derive <pkg>:<path> [--to DIR] [--name N]`: verify the slot, copy the file(s) without overwriting through vibe_safefs, and write the record.
`vibe derive list` / `show <name>`: per-file status `unchanged | modified | deleted | added` against the recorded base hashes.
`vibe derive diff <name>`: three-way status per file (`upstream-changed`, `local-changed`, `both-changed`, `same`) plus unified line diffs for text, using the shared diff helper.

`vibe derive rebase <name>`: dry run by default. `--accept` copies upstream into files the user left unchanged, lists conflicts (both-changed) and leaves them alone, then moves the base pin and base_sha256. A rebase with conflicts records the new base only with `--accept --keep-local`.
`vibe derive remove <name>`: drop the record. Delete only the files whose content still matches the base. `--force` is required for edited files.
Annotate derived paths in `vibe tree` with their origin (crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/tree).
Add CLI integration tests on a fixture registry with two versions of one package.
capabilities.acceptance: In a fixture project with `org.fixture/style@1.0.0` installed: `vibe derive org.fixture/style:templates/ --to local/t` writes byte-identical files and one `[[derived]]` row. After one local file is edited, `show` reports it `modified`. After an upgrade to 1.1.0 that changes a different file, `diff` reports `upstream-changed` for that file and `local-changed` for the edited one. `rebase --accept` updates only the unedited file and moves the base to 1.1.0. Running `derive` again to the same `--to` fails and nothing changes. `vibe tree` shows the `derived from` annotation.
design_decisions: Command: `vibe derive <group/name>:<path-in-package> [--to DIR] [--name NAME]` with subcommands `list`, `show NAME`, `diff NAME`, `rebase NAME [--accept] [--keep-local]`, `remove NAME [--force]`. Use the global `--json` and `--path`.
Default `--to`: `derived/<name>/<last path component>`. Default `--name`: `<package name>-<last path component>`, made unique with a numeric suffix.

Record: vibe.toml `[[derived]]` with `name`, `from = "group/name@=version"`, `path`, `to`, and `base_sha256` (one framed hash over the sorted `path\0sha256` rows, the style of compute_recorded_payload_hash). Per-file base hashes are recomputed from the base bytes, not stored, to keep vibe.toml small.

Old-base bytes: the registry cache at the exact `from` version, through the existing resolver/cache. When they cannot be read offline, report the status `base-unavailable` and fall back to a two-way local-vs-current diff.
Text vs binary: UTF-8 without NUL means text and gets a line diff. Anything else gets hash status only. No Markdown/XML structural merge.

Never overwrite user-edited bytes. A conflict is reported in the result (JSON `conflicts[]`) and the exit code is 0 for a dry run, GENERAL for an `--accept` that left conflicts unresolved without `--keep-local`.
The source must be a dependency installed in this project, read from its verified slot. Refuse when verify_recorded_files fails. Never read `.vibe/cache` skill projections.
capabilities.risks: Overlap and confusion with `[layers]` replace: the docs and `derive --help` must point spec-unit overrides at layers. Reading older versions from the registry cache may need network or fail for removed versions. Adding a manifest section touches a central grammar, so it needs a migration/compat check that older vibe binaries ignore or refuse the section cleanly. `to` paths that land inside the boot lane change agent behaviour. That is intended, but it must be visible in `show`.

capabilities.name: Show and check an authored change against today's project
capabilities.user_story: A user (or agent) who keeps a change under `<spec-root>/changes/<chg-id>/change.toml` runs `vibe change list`, `vibe change show <chg-id>` or `vibe change check [<chg-id>]` (all honour the global `--json`; MCP tool `change_query` returns the same document). `show` prints the change's title, intent and work digests, each declared document with its role and presence, the work items with their needs, and for every need that targets a `spec://` fact the requirements-query axes (authoring, adoption, relations) side by side, never folded into one 'done'. `check` adds drift: every origin citation and captured document hash is reported matched / stale / missing / unavailable against the bytes on disk now, and it exits non-zero on grammar refusals or stale/missing basis so CI can gate on it.
capabilities.todays_form: Thin CLI/MCP adapters over the existing library-only reader `vibe_requirements::change::read_saved_change` + `SavedChange::identity_analysis` (crates/vibe-requirements/src/change/read.rs, identity.rs) and the PROP-071 grammar in crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/change/{mod.rs,work.rs,identity.rs}. The fact axes come from the one constructor `vibe_requirements::query::query` (crates/vibe-requirements/src/query.rs) scoped by each need's address prefix; status words reuse the generated `EvidenceStatus` vocabulary (crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/shared/mod.rs ~3048) and `progress_core::terminal::resolve_terminal`. New `vibe change` subcommand family registered in crates/vibe-cli/src/cli/command.rs next to `Requirements`; MCP tool beside crates/vibe-mcp/src/tools/requirements_query.rs. NOT rebuilt: no second verdict engine, no scheduler, no 'invocation law' types, no M-16 adapter framework; the original 'full-universe join' becomes one pure report function in vibe-requirements.
capabilities.product_question: Is the authored change (PROP-071 change.toml with intent/acceptance/work/closure documents) a user-facing product surface rather than a library-only format?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Yes, starting with this read-only slice: the format, reader and identities are already spec/done and tested, and a read-only show/check is cheap, effect-free and is the only way users ever benefit from that investment.
prerequisites: Merge with the M-02 group's 'change check/show/coverage' remaining behaviour (one task, not two)
rough_steps: Add a pure `vibe_requirements::change::report(selected_root, spec_root, id) -> ChangeReport` that composes read_saved_change, identity_analysis, WorkGraph and per-need requirements query rows
Register a generated wire document `change-report` epoch 1 in formats/REGISTRY.toml with a corpus, mirroring requirements_report
Add origin-drift observation: recompute sha256 of each cited origin document/manifest and classify with EvidenceStatus words
Add `vibe change list|show|check` (crates/vibe-cli/src/cli/change.rs + commands/change.rs) with text and `--json` renderers
Add MCP tool `change_query` (mode list|show|check) calling the same function; parity test asserts byte-identical JSON
Integration tests over the existing formats/corpora/change-manifest fixtures
capabilities.acceptance: On a fixture project with one valid change: `vibe change show chg-... --json` validates against the change-report schema and lists intent/work digests equal to identity_analysis; editing a cited origin document makes `vibe change check` print `stale` for that citation and exit 1; a malformed change.toml exits 1 with the PROP-071 refusal text; MCP `change_query` returns the same JSON as the CLI; no file under the project or .vibe changes (tree hash before == after).
design_decisions: Command family: `vibe change list`, `vibe change show <ID>`, `vibe change check [<ID>]` (no ID = all changes); flags `--path` (default `.`, as in `vibe requirements`) and global `--json`
Spec root: the trusted caller supplies the selected node's configured spec root exactly as read_saved_change already takes it; no new CLI override (PROP-071 forbids the manifest granting a root)

Report fields: `id, title, slug, selected_node, intent_digest, work_digest, documents[{role,path,normative,input,presence}], work[{id,predecessors,needs[{kind,target,fact_rows?}],touches}], origins[{package,manifest_status,documents[{address,status}]}], diagnostics[]`; fact rows are the RequirementRow shape verbatim
Drift vocabulary: reuse EvidenceStatus (matched/missing/stale/unavailable/unstable); no new words

Exit policy: `show` exits 0 whenever the change parses; `check` exits 1 on any refusal, missing normative document, stale or missing origin; `unavailable` is a warning (exit 0) because the origin package may simply not be installed
Read-only law: no install, no sync, no cache write, no network; an uninstalled origin is `unavailable`, never fetched
MCP tool name `change_query` with `mode` enum, one shared core call (CLI/MCP parity is this capability's acceptance, replacing the separate E.2 gate)
Spec home: new units appended to PROP-071 (CHANGE-REPORT, CHANGE-DRIFT) rather than a new PROP
capabilities.risks: Duplicating M-02's planned change report if the two groups are not merged; the requirements query cost if called once per need (batch by prefix); temptation to roll axes into a single 'ready' verdict.

capabilities.name: Create a change and record questions and answers from the CLI
capabilities.user_story: A user runs `vibe change new "Add retry to fetch"` and gets `<spec-root>/changes/chg-<32hex>/` with change.toml, intent.md and acceptance.md templates. While refining it they run `vibe change ask <chg-id> --about spec://org.x/pkg/FEAT-001#RETRY "Should retries apply to POST?"`; the question is stored with the hash of the cited fact's document at ask time. `vibe change answer <chg-id> q-1 "No, idempotent verbs only"` writes `refinements/q-1.md` and declares it as a normative refinement input, so the intent digest changes. `vibe change show` lists open/answered questions and marks a question `stale` when the cited fact's bytes changed after it was asked.
capabilities.todays_form: Extends the PROP-071 change directory and the refinement role that already exists in `ChangeDocumentRole` (crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/change/mod.rs:224). Answers ARE refinement documents (no new answer type); questions are a small record kept in the change directory. Writes go through vibe-safefs owned publication (crates/vibe-safefs) and byte-preserving TOML edits the same way CHANGE-MIGRATION-REPLAY preserves comments and opaque metadata. Staleness reuses the origin-drift check from the show/check capability. NOT rebuilt: no registered-buffer barrier, no M-13/M-16 migration machinery, no editor overlay; dependency packages are never rewritten.
capabilities.product_question: Should vibe write change documents (scaffold, questions, answers), or should authoring stay with the agent/editor and vibe only read and check?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Yes for `new` and `answer` (they fix the hard parts users get wrong: the chg- id grammar and role declarations); ship `ask` in the same slice because it is small once the writer exists.
prerequisites: Show and check an authored change against today's project
rough_steps: Extend PROP-071 with CHANGE-SCAFFOLD and CHANGE-QUESTIONS units and lift the 'no writer' clause for exactly these verbs
Add `questions.toml` format (schema 1, registered in formats/REGISTRY.toml) read by the change reader as a non-normative, non-input file excluded from intent identity
Implement `vibe change new` with generated chg-<32 lowercase hex> id and templates, refusing an existing directory

Implement `vibe change ask` (append q-N with about address, captured sha256 of the cited document, text, asked_at) and `vibe change answer` (write refinements/q-N.md, add a refinement documents row with normative=true input=true, set the question's answer path)
Show open/answered/stale questions in `vibe change show`; MCP tool `change_edit` with the same verbs only if the owner wants agents to write through MCP
capabilities.acceptance: `vibe change new X` then `vibe change check` passes; `ask` then `answer` changes the intent digest reported by `show` and leaves every untouched byte/comment of change.toml identical (diff shows only the added documents row); editing the cited fact's document flips the question to `stale`; an interrupted write (fault-injected) leaves either the old or the new change.toml, never a half-written one; no file outside the change directory is touched.
design_decisions: Verbs: `vibe change new <TITLE> [--slug S]`, `vibe change ask <ID> --about <spec-address> <TEXT>`, `vibe change answer <ID> <QID> <TEXT>|--file <PATH>`
Question ids `q-<n>` monotonically numbered per change; stored in `<change-dir>/questions.toml` (schema 1) not in change.toml, so the strict change.toml epoch 1 grammar is untouched
Answers are refinement documents at `refinements/<qid>.md`, declared normative=true input=true; an answer therefore changes intent identity on purpose
Question states: open | answered | stale (cited bytes changed since ask) | withdrawn (`vibe change ask --withdraw <QID>`)
`--about` must be a spec:// address resolvable in the selected project or an installed origin; an unresolvable address is refused, not stored
Writes: vibe-safefs atomic replace per file; multi-file answer writes the refinement file first, then change.toml, so a crash leaves an undeclared file rather than a dangling declaration
Never write into vibedeps or an origin package; questions about dependency facts are recorded locally only
capabilities.risks: Format growth under PROP-071's strict unknown-field rule (keep questions in a separate file to avoid an epoch bump); overlap with the decision-records flow package (org.vibevm.world/decision-records) which records 'why' at spec anchors; keep questions change-scoped.

capabilities.name: Close a change with retained evidence, waivers and later re-check
capabilities.user_story: When work is done the user runs `vibe change close <chg-id> --as accepted` (or `abandoned`, `superseded --by <chg-id>`), optionally with `--waive spec://...#FACT --reason "..."` / `--accept-risk ...` and `--evidence manual:spec://...#FACT "reviewed by hand"`. vibe writes the declared closure document plus an `evidence/` folder inside the change directory holding copies of the current lifecycle verify report and the change-report, so closure survives deleting `.vibe/`. Later, `vibe change show` on a closed change says 'accepted against intent sha256:A; intent now sha256:B' or 'evidence file missing', keeping the historical decision and the present applicability as separate lines; waived gaps stay listed as waived, never as satisfied.
capabilities.todays_form: Uses the existing `closure` role (derived, non-normative, non-input per PROP-071 CHANGE-DOCUMENT-ROLES) as the closure record, written as TOML at the declared closure path. Evidence copies come from the existing lifecycle verify report (crates/vibe-lifecycle/src/runner/verify*, rendered by crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/lifecycle/report.rs) and the change-report from the show/check capability. Manual/adopted evidence is a closure row with an observer strength, not a fake execution. The applicability re-check reuses identity_analysis and EvidenceStatus. Outside verdicts for progress campaigns stay in `vibe progress gate`/`seal` (crates/vibe-cli/src/cli/progress.rs); the closure may cite a gate record but never stores verdicts of its own. The progress `baseline`/`rescan` pair already gives campaigns 'past verdict vs changed text'; this brings the same idea to changes. NOT rebuilt: no policy engine, no second verdict store, no LLM gate.
capabilities.product_question: Do users need a durable per-change closure record in the repository, separate from progress gates and git history?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Yes if the change workflow is adopted at all: without closure, show/check can never distinguish 'was accepted' from 'is still true', which is the M-04 benefit; keep it after the read slice so demand is proven first.
prerequisites: Show and check an authored change against today's project
rough_steps: Extend PROP-071 with CHANGE-CLOSURE (format, waivers, evidence rows, retention) and CHANGE-APPLICABILITY units
Register `change-closure` TOML format schema 1 with corpus
Implement `vibe change close` writing closure + evidence/ copies with sha256 recorded, refusing when the change has `check` refusals unless every gap is waived
Extend `vibe change show/check` with a closure section: recorded disposition, recorded intent digest vs current, evidence file status, waivers listed separately
Add `--evidence manual|adopted:<address> <detail>` rows with observer strength; MCP `change_query` shows them read-only
capabilities.acceptance: After `vibe change close X --as accepted`, `rm -rf .vibe` and `vibe change show X` still prints the closure and evidence as matched; editing intent.md makes `show` print both the historical acceptance and 'intent changed' without rewriting closure; a waived fact appears under `waived` and `vibe requirements` output for that fact is unchanged; `close` on a change with an unwaived missing normative document exits 1; `vibe progress gate` records are untouched.
design_decisions: Verb: `vibe change close <ID> --as accepted|abandoned|superseded [--by <ID>] [--waive <ADDR> --reason <TEXT>]... [--accept-risk <ADDR> --reason <TEXT>]... [--evidence <manual|adopted>:<ADDR> <TEXT>]...`
Closure path: the document declared with role=closure in change.toml; if none is declared, `close` adds `closure.toml` with normative=false input=false

Closure fields: `disposition, superseded_by?, closed_at, intent_digest, work_digest, [[waivers]]{address,kind=waiver|accepted-risk,reason}, [[evidence]]{subject,observer=executed|manual|adopted,file?,sha256?,detail}`
Retained evidence lives in `<change-dir>/evidence/` (committed with the change), never only in `.vibe/`
Re-close is refused unless `--reopen` first clears it; a closure is never edited in place by show/check
Waivers never change the neutral requirements query; they appear only in the change report under their own key
Closure bytes are excluded from intent identity (already PROP-071 law) so closing never alters what was accepted

capabilities.name: Verify a create step that edits an existing source file
capabilities.user_story: When an agentic `vibe create` step rewrites a file inside its own declared scope, `vibe verify` reports that file as produced by that execution (not `stale`), and the following build and test phases run on the new bytes; an unrelated edit to the same file by someone else is still reported as stale.
capabilities.todays_form: Extends vibe-lifecycle verify (crates/vibe-lifecycle/src/runner/verify/inputs.rs, artifacts.rs) and state checkpoints with a per-step pre/post hash of declared existing-file outputs; no universal transition ledger.

capabilities.acceptance: Integration test: create agent rewrites a declared file; `vibe verify` shows it as produced by that run and build/test consume the new bytes; an out-of-band edit after the step shows stale.
design_decisions: Owner: M-11-D; M-03 contributes the verify-report wording only
capabilities.risks: Duplicate planning across M-03 and M-11; universal ledger creep.

capabilities.name: Uninstall a configured package
capabilities.user_story: A user who configured a dependency under [requires.configurations] runs `vibe uninstall org.x/driver`. Vibe removes the [requires.packages] entry, the [requires.configurations] entry, the vibe.lock configurations record, the slot and every dependency the configuration selected that no other root still holds, then rebuilds boot. Removing a package that some other configured owner selected refuses with a hint like `org.x/extra is selected by org.x/driver feature "extra"; turn that feature off in [requires.configurations."org.x/driver"] or uninstall org.x/driver`.
capabilities.todays_form: Extends the existing uninstall command: crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/uninstall.rs (lines ~75-86 hold the blanket 'configuration-aware removal is not connected' refusal) and uninstall/plan.rs (drop_requires already removes r.configurations at l.212; closure() computes the reverse closure). Lockfile::remove-style helper at crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/lockfile.rs:562 already drops lock.configurations[key]. Dependency attribution comes from PackageConfiguration.active_dependencies / dependency_causes (crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/configuration/package.rs). Not rebuilt: no generic recovery journal, no new uninstall transaction; the existing uninstall transaction is reused. Moving uninstall behind vibe-install (BACKLOG NST P2 row 5) and adding a lifecycle lease (row 15) are separate consolidation.
rough_steps: Narrow the refusal: allow when the target itself is the configured owner; keep refusal only when a removed row is an active_dependency of a configured owner that stays installed.
Include the owner's active_dependencies as closure seeds so selected-only deps not held by other roots are removed; remove lock.configurations[owner].
Replace the generic refusal text for the retained-owner case with an actionable message naming owner, feature (from dependency_causes) and the vibe.toml table to edit.
Rewrite boundaries.rs:89 test to assert successful removal (vibe.toml, lock, slots, boot) and add a test for the selected-dependency refusal message.
capabilities.acceptance: cargo test -p vibe-cli --test cli_common_package_optional boundaries: `vibe uninstall DRIVER` exits 0; vibe.toml lacks both requires and configurations entries; vibe.lock configurations lacks DRIVER; DRIVER slot and unshared oracle-extra slot are gone; static boot lacks DRIVER_MARKER; unrelated root and its bytes unchanged. `vibe uninstall oracle-extra` while DRIVER keeps it selected exits non-zero before any write, naming DRIVER and the feature.
design_decisions: No new flag: uninstall of a configured owner just works; no --force path for removing a selected dependency.

Selected-dependency refusal is a PackageConfigurationError::Unsupported-free typed error: 'X is selected by configured package Y (feature F); disable F in [requires.configurations."Y"] or uninstall Y'. Exit code GENERAL, nothing written.
A dependency still reached by another root (legacy or configured) is retained, same rule as today's closure.
If the owner's record is missing or inconsistent with the lock, refuse before effects (reuse rich_missing_record refusal wording) rather than guessing the closure.
capabilities.risks: Closure must use the lock's actual edges plus active_dependencies, not re-evaluate the configuration; forwarded inputs from the removed owner into a shared dependency's record must be handled (refuse if another consumer's record still references forwarded input, rather than silently rewriting it). Verify manual workaround (edit vibe.toml, vibe install) first so the test baseline is right.

capabilities.name: Legacy feature flags are applied and replayed
capabilities.user_story: A user runs `vibe install --features extra` on a project whose lock is fresh. Today vibe prints 'vibe.lock is fresh' and activates nothing. After this ships the flag forces a resolve, `extra` is active and recorded in vibe.lock, and vibe prints a note that flags live only in the lock and that [requires.configurations] is the durable place. A later `vibe reinstall` replays the locked root features instead of dropping them.
capabilities.todays_form: crates/vibe-install/src/plan/fresh.rs freshness_prepared (l.62-117) already refuses flags mixed with configured input (configured::mixed_flags); add one rule: any of request.features.{all,no_defaults,explicit} on an unconfigured project returns Freshness::Stale("feature flags require resolution"). crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/reinstall/inputs.rs:~95 hard-codes features: Vec::new(); fill it from lock packages[root].features / meta.active_features (crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/lockfile.rs:231,473). Multi-consumer/intent-only freshness (configuration_freshness) is already delivered and not touched.
rough_steps: In freshness_prepared return Stale when any legacy feature flag is present and no configured input exists.
Emit a one-line note after install when legacy flags were used: features recorded in vibe.lock only.
In reinstall inputs, replay root features from the lock rather than an empty list.
Add vibe-cli integration tests: fresh lock + --features extra activates extra; reinstall keeps it.
capabilities.acceptance: New vibe-cli test: install root with [features] non-default `extra` activating a dependency; `vibe install --features extra` does not print 'vibe.lock is fresh', lock packages[root].features contains extra, dependency slot exists; `vibe reinstall` afterwards keeps extra and the dependency slot.
design_decisions: Policy: flags force Stale (apply), not refuse; refusal only remains for mixing with configured input (existing mixed_flags).
Stale reason text: 'legacy feature flags require resolution'.
Reinstall replays the locked features exactly; it does not read flags from the command line (reinstall takes none).
Do not write flags into vibe.toml; durable intent stays [requires.configurations].
capabilities.risks: A plain later `vibe install` without flags on a stale lock may drop flag-only features; that is the existing legacy semantics and the note warns about it. Do not redesign legacy features.

capabilities.name: Redbook continuity as a package choice
capabilities.user_story: A Redbook consumer chooses its continuity model in vibe.toml, e.g. `[requires.configurations."org.vibevm.world/redbook"] continuity = "multi-user-planning"`, instead of a hand-maintained `exclude` list. `vibe show configuration-preview org.vibevm.world/redbook` lists the WAL and multi-user-planning options; `vibe install` loads only the chosen family, `vibe update` keeps the choice, and the other family's choice survives as dormant input. Consumers that still use `exclude` keep working.
capabilities.todays_form: A new Redbook version under vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.world/redbook (v1.0.0 slot is immutable) declares a [configuration] group (one-of: wal | multi-user-planning) using the existing kernel (crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/configuration). The host vibe.toml (l.25-31) replaces its exclude with a configurations entry by a manual edit (no migrator). C.3 becomes real: configured owners with an `exclude` mask refuse at crates/vibe-resolver/src/source_solve/metadata.rs:65 and configuration/provider.rs:86; that refusal must be widened (mask applied with provenance) so external consumers' exclude keeps working. G.2's coexistence proof is just this capability's acceptance; prefix-failure recovery is already covered by refuse_before_effects tests.
capabilities.product_question: Approve a new Redbook version (and its publication cascade, B-067/B-181) whose continuity family is selected by a configuration group?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Yes, but only together with the exclude-mask widening: it is the first real dogfood of package configuration (no vibepack declares [configuration] today), and without it the whole M-05 machinery has no shipped user.
rough_steps: Owner approves the Redbook version bump.
Widen the configured-owner exclude refusal: apply the visibility mask after evaluation, record masked declarations in the configuration record.
Author the new Redbook version with a one-of continuity group, default matching today's unconfigured behaviour.
Edit host vibe.toml to use the configuration instead of exclude; reinstall.
Tests: WAL-only, MUP-only, exclude-legacy consumer, switch-and-back retains dormant choice.
capabilities.acceptance: Two fixture consumers (one choosing wal, one multi-user-planning) each boot only their family; a third with the old exclude list installs identically to today; host `vibe install` then `vibe check` clean; `vibe update` with unchanged choice is fresh.

Default = today's unconfigured Redbook contents to keep existing consumers byte-stable.
Exclude on a configured owner: apply mask (not refuse); masked items listed in the configuration record under declarations provenance.
Host consumer migration is a hand edit; no automated migrator dependency.

After this ships the solve picks the alternative and the lock records which edge was selected.

Remove the refusal for the projected kinds; keep installer requirements refusing if projection is unclear.
Fixture tests for each requirement kind with cold replay.

capabilities.name: Smoke the installed bootstrap on every release target
capabilities.user_story: When a maintainer dispatches release-distributions.yml, each of the five native build jobs (Windows x86_64, Linux musl, Linux GNU, macOS Intel, macOS ARM64) runs the same init + install flow:wal + tree smoke against the exact bootstrap it just built, before the bundle is retained and uploaded. A bootstrap broken on any platform fails its own job and never reaches the draft release, so Linux and Windows users can no longer download a bootstrap that was only proven on Intel macOS.
capabilities.todays_form: Extends the existing step 'Smoke Intel macOS portable-flow materialization' in .github/workflows/release-distributions.yml (today gated by `if: matrix.target == 'x86_64-apple-darwin'`, ~lines 229-246). The step body moves into two repo scripts beside the existing per-target build scripts in distribution/release/, so a maintainer can run the same smoke locally on any built bootstrap. NOT built: the original reusable native smoke harness, Docker executor (M-15-K.1), per-target evidence records, skip-evidence policy, remote interruption-rehearsal matrix. B.2's 'default-on' intent reduces to: the smoke is unconditional and has no skip switch. xtask dist finalize already digest-binds what was smoked to what is published (finalize_with + verify_platform_bytes).
capabilities.product_question: Do you approve this edit to the release CI workflow (Rule 4 ask-first: CI change)?

capabilities.name: Verifiable producer provenance for release bundles
capabilities.user_story: Every bundle and bootstrap attached to a GitHub release carries a GitHub build-provenance attestation, so a security-minded user can run `gh attestation verify vibe-bootstrap-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --repo <owner>/vibevm` and see that it was built by this repository's release workflow from the tagged commit, not only that its sha256 matches the manifest. capabilities.name: Bridge skills that actually run: reference closure warning and executable scripts
capabilities.user_story: A user installs a bridge such as org.speckit/speckit and runs `vibe skill install`. The scripts and templates the projected commands invoke are present, and shell scripts keep their executable bit, so the agent can run them. If a projected SKILL.md or command file references a relative script or template path that exists neither in the projected skill tree nor in the project, `vibe skill install` prints `warning: skill speckit-core references scripts/bash/check-prerequisites.sh, which is not shipped`. Package authors see this before users do. After a warm cache, the whole journey works with VIBE_OFFLINE=1.
capabilities.todays_form: This extends the existing composed-tree projection in crates/vibe-agent-projection/src/pkgskill/projection.rs (hydrate_declared_skill ~:339, [[skill.resource]] composition :345-393) and its receipts (pkgskill/receipt). Two changes: (1) after the tree is composed, a pure scan collects unresolved relative references and returns them as warnings through the existing install report. (2) The projection keeps the source file's Unix executable bit and records it in the receipt file entry. The old 'audit of the resource closure' (A.1) becomes this automated scan. The old 'typed admitted script action route' (C.2) is replaced by 'scripts arrive runnable': the agent executes them as today, and Vibe never runs foreign procedures. The offline journey (E.1) is the acceptance. Not rebuilt: no foreign-resource interpretation layer, no core action engine, no change to [[embedded_source]] authentication. The actual missing Spec Kit content is fixed in the external org.speckit/speckit repository.

It considers markdown link targets and backticked tokens that contain '/', have a file extension, are not URLs, and do not start with '/' or '~'.
Surface the result as non-fatal warnings in `vibe skill install` output and in its --json report as an `unresolved_references` array per skill.

Keep the executable bit on Unix when writing projected files (std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt), check that the embedded-source cache keeps the mode bit, add a `mode`/`executable` field to the receipt file entry with serde default false for old receipts, and treat a mode change as an update rather than drift.

Add unit tests: a fixture bridge with a SKILL.md referencing an existing script, a missing script and a URL gives exactly one warning; a projected 0755 script stays executable; an old receipt without the field still uninstalls.
In the external org.speckit/speckit repo (owner approval needed to publish), add the helper scripts and templates as [[skill.resource]] entries until the warning list is empty.

Acceptance run: warm the cache, then with VIBE_OFFLINE=1 and a scratch project run `vibe skill install` for both bridges, get zero warnings, and run one projected Spec Kit script with `--help`/`--json`.
capabilities.acceptance: `cargo test -p vibe-agent-projection pkgskill::closure` and the receipt mode tests pass. Running `vibe skill install` on a fixture bridge with a dangling reference prints exactly one warning naming the skill and path, and exits 0. With the fixed Spec Kit bridge: VIBE_OFFLINE=1 install gives zero warnings, `test -x .claude/skills/<skill>/scripts/bash/<script>.sh` succeeds, and the script runs.
design_decisions: Severity: a warning only, never an error, and the exit code is unchanged, because the heuristic can produce false positives.
Resolution order for a reference: the skill's own projected dir, then the project root. Found in either means resolved.

Reference grammar: markdown `[..](path)` targets and inline-code tokens matching ^(\.{0,2}/)?[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)+\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$. URLs, absolute paths, ~ paths and paths containing '<', '{' or '$' are ignored.
Only .md files in the composed tree are scanned.
JSON field: `unresolved_references: [{skill, file, reference}]` in the existing skill-install JSON report. The human line is `warning: skill <name> (<file>) references <ref>, which is not shipped`.
Mode: only the owner-execute bit is propagated, as 0o755 or 0o644. On Windows it is a no-op. The receipt field is `executable: bool` with #[serde(default)].

Spec Kit's `.specify/...` project-root paths are resolved against the project root. If the bridge needs `.specify/` materialised into the project, that is package content (an installed project file), not a new core feature.
capabilities.risks: Spec Kit commands reference project-root `.specify/` paths, not skill-relative ones, so the external fix may need the package to rewrite paths or ship a project-file payload. Verify against the real upstream before promising zero warnings. It is not yet verified whether the embedded-source cache keeps the mode bits (git tree mode 100755 should carry them). Check that before step 3. Republishing the external bridge changes remote state and needs the owner's approval.
