design_decisions: Do not add a fourth enum variant and call it extensibility.
Do not create a descriptor schema separate from the consolidation owner.
capabilities.risks: Building a generic grant system before any consumer exists. Merging with the 8-agent enum unification without an owner decision.

capabilities.name: Detect the stack of an existing project in vibe init
capabilities.user_story: In an existing repository a user runs `vibe init --detect-stack --plan-only` and sees, without any write, the stacks vibe recognises (e.g. `rust-ai-native` because `Cargo.toml` is at the root), the evidence file for each, the existing agent files (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md) that will be kept with only a marked block added, the files init would create, and any skipped or unreadable paths. Running `vibe init --detect-stack` then initializes the project with that stack recorded and prints the exact `vibe install` command to run next. `--json` gives the same proposal to the user's coding agent.
capabilities.todays_form: Extends `vibe init` (crates/vibe-cli/src/cli/init.rs InitArgs; crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/init/mod.rs create_project) with a new module crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/init/detect.rs. The scope walk reuses the vibe-safefs no-follow Project API exactly as crates/vibe-scrape/src/inventory.rs does (second listing to report a changing directory). Writing stays with today's init: it already skips existing files (init/helpers.rs:276,339), and boot regeneration only splices the generated <vibevm> block into existing CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md (crates/vibe-workspace/src/boot_artifacts/redirect.rs). Installing stays `vibe install`. NOT rebuilt: no separate inventory crate, no promotion planner or transaction (the C.1/C.2 form), no LLM operation in vibe-llm (B.2 becomes agent-readable JSON with evidence and assumptions), no generic analyzer framework, and `vibe scrape` is not touched or renamed.
capabilities.product_question: Should onboarding an existing repository detect its stack and propose the published ai-native stack package, instead of the user typing `--stack` by hand?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Yes, limited to the three published stacks (rust, typescript, go). It is the only M-11 piece a user notices, and it reuses init and install unchanged.
rough_steps: Add detect.rs: a bounded root-level marker scan (depth <= 2, excluding .git, vibevm/, target/, node_modules/) over the vibe-safefs no-follow API that returns detected stacks with evidence paths and skipped/unstable paths
Add `--detect-stack` (conflicts with `--stack`) and `--plan-only` to InitArgs. `--plan-only` prints the proposal and writes nothing
List the existing agent instruction files and how each is handled (kept, with a generated block added) in the proposal
Without `--plan-only`, run the existing create_project with the detected stack in [active].stack and print `next_commands`
With several or no matches: in an attended TTY ask the user to choose with the existing prompts module, otherwise refuse with a typed reason. Never guess
Add a CLI integration test on Cargo, package.json and go.mod fixtures plus a mixed fixture, with JSON golden output and a check that the existing CLAUDE.md text is byte-preserved outside the markers
capabilities.acceptance: `vibe init --detect-stack --plan-only --json` in a fixture with Cargo.toml and a hand-written CLAUDE.md exits 0, prints stack `rust-ai-native` with evidence `Cargo.toml`, lists CLAUDE.md as `keep`, and leaves the tree byte-identical (tree digest before = after). `vibe init --detect-stack` in the same fixture writes vibe.toml with `[active] stack = "rust-ai-native"`, keeps the CLAUDE.md user text verbatim outside the <vibevm> block, and prints `vibe install stack:org.vibevm.ai-native/rust-ai-native`. A fixture with Cargo.toml and package.json under `--unattended` exits non-zero with the reason `ambiguous-stack` and lists both candidates.
design_decisions: Flags: `--detect-stack` (bool, conflicts_with `stack`) and `--plan-only` (bool, requires `detect-stack`). `--plan-only` matches the existing name in crates/vibe-cli/src/cli/pkg.rs:197; no `--propose` or `--dry-run`

Detection table is built in, in detect.rs: Cargo.toml -> org.vibevm.ai-native/rust-ai-native; package.json or tsconfig.json -> org.vibevm.ai-native/typescript-ai-native; go.mod -> org.vibevm.ai-native/go-ai-native. Markers declared by stack packages in their own manifests are deferred until a third-party stack asks for them

Scan scope: the project root and one level below, no symlink following, excluding .git, vibevm, target, node_modules and dist. A changed directory listing or an unreadable entry is reported in `skipped[]` with reason `unstable` or `unreadable`, never fatal

JSON proposal fields: `stacks[] {coordinate, name, evidence[]}`, `agent_files[] {path, action: keep|create}`, `writes[] {path, action}`, `skipped[] {path, reason}`, `assumptions[]`, `next_commands[]`. The JSON goes through the existing output::Context envelope
[active].stack records the package name (`rust-ai-native`), the shape `--stack` already writes. init never installs

Ambiguity or no match: attended -> choose via commands/init/prompts.rs; unattended/JSON -> exit with typed reason `ambiguous-stack` / `no-stack-detected` (no-stack-detected under --plan-only is exit 0 with empty stacks)
A project that already has vibe.toml: refuse `--detect-stack` without `--plan-only`, with the same message root_role.rs gives for an existing manifest
capabilities.risks: Scope creep into an analyzer framework or an LLM call. Keep it to a table. typescript vs plain JS is guessed from package.json and must be listed as an assumption. Coordinate with NST-DOMAIN-CONSOLIDATION P3 row 13 (prompt routing in init/scrape files).

capabilities.name: Lifecycle verify says when a producer rewrote its own input
capabilities.user_story: When `vibe lifecycle verify` reports an input row as stale, the user can tell whether the change came from the producer's own last run or from someone else. The row carries reason `input-rewritten-by-producer` when the observed bytes are exactly what the recorded run wrote, and no reason (as today) for a foreign edit.
capabilities.todays_form: Extends the existing per-row reason vocabulary in crates/vibe-lifecycle/src/runner/verify/inputs.rs (refusal(), DECLARATION_CHANGED) by comparing the observed witness against the artifact witness recorded under the same measured_run_id (runner/verify/artifacts.rs). No new wire field: reason_code already exists on InputMeasurement (crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/shared/mod.rs:3198). NOT rebuilt: no universal transition recipe or ledger (M-11-D.1), and matching bytes never grant authority (status stays stale).
capabilities.product_question: Does any current lifecycle producer declare a file as both an input and an output?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Check the installed lifecycle declarations first. If none does, do not build, because the reason code would never appear.
rough_steps: Find the run's recorded artifact witnesses for the same path and measured_run_id
When the row is stale and the observed digest equals that artifact witness, set reason_code `input-rewritten-by-producer`
Register the code in the reason vocabulary and the schema docs
Add a runner test: a producer rewrites its input, verify shows the reason, and a later foreign edit shows no reason
capabilities.acceptance: `cargo test -p vibe-lifecycle runner::tests` includes a test where a producer rewrites its declared input: verify reports status `stale` with reason_code `input-rewritten-by-producer`. After a foreign edit of the same file, the reason code is absent and the status is stale.
design_decisions: Reason code spelling: `input-rewritten-by-producer`, kebab-case like `input-unstable`
Status stays `stale`, never `matched`: the reason explains the change and does not excuse it
Attribution only against the witness of the same measured_run_id, never against any earlier run
capabilities.risks: Value depends on producers that write their own inputs. Possibly zero today.

capabilities.name: Plain one-command manifest migration for people
capabilities.user_story: A user whose vibe.toml uses a legacy shape runs `vibe refactor migrate-manifest` and sees a readable diff of the planned token edits, with comments kept. They answer any typed question in the terminal, then run it again with `--apply`, which writes through the guarded migration runtime and prints the restore command. Today this is possible only by writing JSON requests for `plan-migration` and `migration-operation`.
capabilities.todays_form: A thin human front over the accepted owners: vibe_core::manifest::plan_manifest_migration via crates/vibe-workspace/src/migration_planning.rs, and crates/vibe-workspace/src/migration_application (apply/inspect/restore, recovery store). The new verb lives beside PlanMigration/MigrationOperation in crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/refactor/mod.rs. NOT rebuilt: no new planner, no new recovery store format, and the JSON verbs and MCP tools stay as they are.
capabilities.product_question: Do real users or the corporate kit still hold manifests in a legacy profile (materialization-legacy-absent-r1, source-boot-normal-absent-r1, snapshot-to-copy-r1) that the reader asks them to migrate?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Build only if a scan of the public vibepacks and the corporate kit inputs finds such manifests. Otherwise the JSON surface already used by agents is enough.
rough_steps: Add `migrate-manifest [PATH]` (default ./vibe.toml), which reads the file and plans it with the default selection
Render outcomes: no-op, a planned unified diff, needs-input (attended prompts, unattended exit with the question list), refused (typed reason)
`--apply` grants project_root and target_relative from PATH and uses the default recovery store under the settings home, then calls the migration_application runtime
Print `vibe refactor migrate-manifest --restore <operation-id>` after an apply
Add CLI tests: comments preserved, a stale input refused, and a restore that returns the original bytes
capabilities.acceptance: In a fixture with a legacy-profile vibe.toml that has comments, `vibe refactor migrate-manifest` exits 0, prints a diff and leaves the file unchanged. `--apply` rewrites only the planned tokens, keeps the comments, and prints an operation id. `--restore <id>` returns the original bytes exactly. Editing the file between plan and apply makes `--apply` refuse with the existing stale-input refusal.
design_decisions: Verb: `vibe refactor migrate-manifest [PATH]`, with flags `--apply`, `--restore <OPERATION_ID>`, `--recovery-store <DIR>` and global `--json`
The default recovery store is `<settings>/state/migrations/` and must stay outside the project, as the runtime requires
Without `--apply` the command is read-only. Plan identity is recomputed at apply time and compared, so the existing refusal path is reused
The JSON mode emits the existing plan-report / migration-operation-report formats unchanged
capabilities.risks: There may be no legacy manifests in the wild. Native macOS/Windows qualification of the runtime remains unexecuted and belongs to platform qualification.

capabilities.name: Plan an application for another target root without touching the host
capabilities.user_story: A user runs `vibe app plan <pkg> --target-root ./rootfs --target-platform linux --target-arch x86_64` and sees the same package identity and choices as the host plan, with each effect labelled by destination: target path, needs a target executor, or impossible. `vibe app install <pkg> --target-root ./rootfs` refuses before any host write, saying no executor is admitted for that target. A target root that resolves to the host settings home or the project home is refused, because a path string is not permission to change that directory.
capabilities.todays_form: Extends the existing PROP-065 plan surface: `vibe app plan` (crates/vibe-cli/src/cli/app.rs:171), crates/vibe-app/src/operations/planning.rs::plan and OperationContext (operations/mod.rs:75), with a target binding beside SettingsRoot (crates/vibe-app/src/settings.rs) rather than a fake HOME. It adds optional target fields to the existing application_plan wire family (crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/application_plan) instead of a new environment schema family. Platform/arch tokens reuse SUPPORTED_DISTRIBUTION_TARGETS (crates/vibe-wire/src/behaviour/release_manifest.rs:81). Alias refusal reuses the canonicalized home check in MutationLock::require_home (settings.rs). NOT rebuilt: none of the prototype types (EnvironmentDefinition, TargetInstanceId, DeclaredRootBinding, acquire_destination), no environment lock or realization closure, no Docker/OCI, and no second store.
capabilities.product_question: Does the owner accept BACKLOG B233's direction (environments and rootfs prepared through the existing `vibe install -g`/app meta-distribution) enough to ship a plan-only target slice?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Yes, plan-only. It is the disposition's first discriminating journey, it is read-only with refusal, and it tests the B233 hypothesis without committing to image or executor support.
prerequisites: owner ruling on BACKLOG B233
rough_steps: Add a TargetBinding value (root path, platform, arch, principal=none) to vibe-app with absent meaning the host, never inferred from a path
Thread an optional target through OperationContext into planning, and label each step's effect with destination kind and target-visible path
Add the optional `target` block to the application_plan wire format and its corpus, and render it in the CLI plan view
Refuse a target root whose canonical path equals or is inside the settings home, the install root or the project home
`vibe app install --target-root` refuses with `target-executor-unavailable` before taking the MutationLock or writing anything
Add a CLI test that plans the same fixture app for the host and for a synthetic rootfs, diffs the destinations, and shows the install refusal leaves the host tree untouched
capabilities.acceptance: In a fixture registry with a small app, `vibe app plan app --json` and `vibe app plan app --target-root <tmp>/rootfs --target-platform linux --target-arch x86_64 --json` report the same package identity and option id, and every effect in the second has `destination.kind` = target|needs-executor|impossible with paths under the rootfs. `vibe app install app --target-root <tmp>/rootfs` exits non-zero with `target-executor-unavailable`, and the settings home and rootfs digests are unchanged. `--target-root $VIBE_SETTINGS` exits with `target-aliases-host-home`.
design_decisions: Flags on `vibe app plan` and `vibe app install`: `--target-root <DIR>`, `--target-platform <ID>`, `--target-arch <ID>`. `--target-root` is required for the other two. The existing host `--platform/--arch` keep their meaning
An absent target means the host, and legacy records and plans without `target` are read as the host. Nothing is upgraded by decoding (B.2 intent)

Wire: an optional `target {root, platform, arch}` on the plan root plus a per-effect `destination {kind: host|target|needs-executor|impossible, path?}`. A version bump of the application_plan format follows the existing wire epoch rules
Error codes are added to crates/vibe-app/src/error_catalog.rs: `target-executor-unavailable`, `target-aliases-host-home`, `target-platform-unsupported`
Host launchers/PATH exposure steps for a target are labelled `impossible`, never published into the operator's PATH
The rootfs need not exist for plan. A missing directory is reported, not created
capabilities.risks: Pulling in effects (C.3) or Docker claims early. Overlap with M-15 realization and with the corporate kit's producer-host vs consumer-target vocabulary (KIT-CROSS-TARGET), so share platform tokens and do not fork them. Windows hosts must not claim Linux target support beyond planning.

capabilities.name: Install a builtin into a bound user-profile root
capabilities.user_story: After the plan-only slice, a user can actually install a `vibe-bin` builtin into an explicitly bound second user-profile root (e.g. a mounted rootfs home) with `vibe app install <pkg> --target-root <dir> --executor host`. The receipt names the bound root, and a rerun detects that the root was swapped or aliased in the meantime and refuses.
capabilities.todays_form: Threads the TargetBinding from the plan-only capability through the incumbent deploy transaction in crates/vibe-lifecycle/src/mechanism/deploy (protocol.rs, ownership.rs, transaction.rs, sidecar.rs) with a held vibe-safefs root and lease/locks from crates/vibe-lifecycle/src/lease.rs. The receipt gets the bound-root identity. NOT rebuilt: no second package manager or store, no image build, no executor beyond `host` for same-OS roots.
capabilities.product_question: After the plan-only slice, does the owner want real writes into non-host roots (the first step toward rootfs/container preparation under B233)?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Not yet. Decide after the plan-only slice shows the destinations are right and a concrete container journey is chosen.
prerequisites: Plan an application for another target root without touching the host
rough_steps: Add an `--executor host` admission valid only when the target platform equals the host platform
Hold the target root through vibe-safefs and record its identity in the deploy intent and receipt
Before the first write and before commit, recheck the root identity and generation, and refuse on a swap or alias
Add CLI tests for install into a temp root, the receipt, a swapped-root refusal, and uninstall from the bound root
capabilities.acceptance: `vibe app install bin-fixture --target-root <tmp>/root --executor host` writes only under <tmp>/root, and its receipt records the root identity. Replacing <tmp>/root with a symlink to another dir before a rerun makes the rerun refuse with `target-root-changed`. The host settings home digest is unchanged throughout.
design_decisions: `--executor host` is the only executor and requires target platform = host platform
Error code `target-root-changed` is added to the app error catalog
The receipt stores the bound root's canonical path plus its vibe-safefs native identity. A pathname match alone never authorizes a write
capabilities.risks: This is the start of B233 product scope, and an XL tail (OCI, hooks, services) can grow behind it.

capabilities.name: `vibe bin` runs the newest build, not whichever debug build exists
capabilities.user_story: A package author runs `vibe bin build rust-ai-native` after editing code. `vibe bin exec rust-ai-native`, `vibe bin path` and the MCP server registered from the package now start that new release build. Before this change, a debug binary left over from an older `cargo build` in the slot silently won. `vibe bin list` shows which profile is selected and marks a stale artifact, for example `built (release, newer than debug)`.
capabilities.todays_form: Change `DeclaredBinary::artifact()` in crates/vibe-workspace/src/bins.rs:249. Today it returns `debug_artifact()` whenever that file exists. All callers go through it: crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/bin.rs (run_path, run_exec, run_list) and crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/mcp/package_registration.rs. The debug-first rule lives only in the doc comment (bins.rs:207-222) and in the test `artifact_prefers_debug_over_release` (bins/tests.rs:96). The PROP-025 `#dispatch` text says nothing about debug, so the spec needs at most one new fact line. Nothing new is built: no closure record and no artifact database. The original 'trusted substitution' half is dropped because nothing uses it.
rough_steps: Change artifact(): when both debug and release exist, return the one with the newer mtime. When only one exists, return it.
Add `DeclaredBinary::selected_profile()` returning debug or release, and print it in the `vibe bin list` row and its JSON output
Rewrite `artifact_prefers_debug_over_release` as `artifact_prefers_newest_build`, with a case for older debug plus newer release and the reverse case
Add a DISPATCH-FRESHEST fact to PROP-025 #dispatch and point the #[spec] marker at it
capabilities.acceptance: `cargo test -p vibe-workspace --lib bins::tests` passes the new freshness cases. In a slot that holds an older target/debug/<name> and a newer target/release/<name>, `vibe bin path <name>` prints the release path and `vibe bin list --json` reports profile "release".
design_decisions: Rule: pick the newest by filesystem mtime. Reading a build record is not needed because `vibe bin build` writes the release artifact through cargo.
Tie or unreadable mtime: prefer debug. This keeps today's behaviour for developers who are iterating.
No new flag. An explicit choice can come later as `vibe bin exec --profile debug|release` if someone asks for it; it is out of scope here.
`vibe bin list` human column: `built (debug)` / `built (release)`. JSON gets a new field `profile`, added only (no existing field changes).
No warning on stderr for `bin exec`, because its stdout and stderr belong to the child process. The information goes in `vibe bin list` only.
capabilities.risks: mtime can be wrong after a copy or checkout (for example a vendored slot copied with mtimes preserved). This is low impact because both artifacts were built from the same slot source.

capabilities.name: Plan apps into a separate root filesystem, refusing when no executor is available
capabilities.user_story: A user runs `vibe app plan ripgrep --target rootfs:./img-root --platform linux --arch x86_64`, or `vibe app import apps.vibe-apps --target rootfs:./img-root --plan-only`. They see the same package identity, installer choice and features as the host plan, but every effect is labelled with its destination: target path, host cache, or 'needs executor'. Asking to apply it either places payloads under ./img-root (archive-only installers, with no hooks) or refuses with `no Linux executor available (docker not found)` before touching the host. `vibe app executor check` reports whether Docker or another Linux builder is usable.
capabilities.todays_form: This is the first journey in the environment-target disposition (campaigns/next-semantic-transfer-2026-11/research/environment-target-design-disposition.md). It extends the existing planner `vibe_app::operations::planning::plan` (crates/vibe-app/src/operations/planning.rs:10) and the `vibe app plan` command (crates/vibe-cli/src/cli/app.rs:171, which already takes --platform/--arch). It carries the target as a new field on `OperationContext` (operations/mod.rs:75). Payloads are unpacked by the existing archive realizer crates/vibe-app/src/installer/archive.rs, which already keeps links and modes. The environment definition is the existing `vibe-apps/1` set (crates/vibe-app/src/portable.rs:62, `vibe app export`/`import`); there is no new lock grammar. NOT built: an immutable store, generations, a second planner, a Dockerfile generator, running target hooks on the host, or publishing a target launcher onto the operator's PATH.
capabilities.product_question: Approve B-233 (Vibe's meta-distribution extended to non-HOME targets such as a rootfs or container) as a product direction, starting with rootfs planning?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Yes, but only this slice first. It reuses the existing planner, proves or disproves the B-233 hypothesis cheaply, and its refusal path is safe.
prerequisites: Owner decision on B-233
M-14 target identity / root binding (at least an injected layout so storage and paths can resolve against a non-HOME root)
rough_steps: Add `InstallTarget { Host, Rootfs { root, platform, arch } }` to OperationContext, defaulting to Host. Thread it through planning.rs so each plan step carries a destination label
`vibe app plan --target rootfs:<dir>` prints the labelled plan. Steps that need running code in the target are marked `needs-executor`
`vibe app executor check` performs a pure detection of a docker CLI and daemon and reports the result. It is cached for the current process only
Applying to a rootfs: archive-only options are realized under <dir> through installer/archive.rs. Any step labelled needs-executor refuses with a typed error before any host mutation
`vibe app import <set> --target rootfs:<dir>` accepts a vibe-apps/1 set as the environment definition
Test: the same app planned for host and for rootfs shows identical choices and different destinations, and with no executor the rootfs apply refuses and leaves the host index unchanged
capabilities.acceptance: `vibe app plan <small-archive-app> --target rootfs:$T --json` shows the same option and features as the host plan, with destination fields under $T. `vibe app install <app-with-hook> --target rootfs:$T` exits non-zero with code `executor-unavailable` while ~/.vibe app index and PATH stay byte-identical. `vibe app executor check --json` reports `{docker: available|missing|daemon-down}`.
design_decisions: Flag spelling: `--target rootfs:<dir>` (scheme-prefixed, so later `image:<ref>` and `host` fit the same flag). Default is `host`.
The target root must be an existing empty directory or one that a previous `--target` run already wrote. A marker file `<root>/.vibe-target.toml` records this; refuse otherwise.
Target index and receipts live inside the target at `<root>/var/lib/vibe/` (target-visible), never in the host ~/.vibe index. Downloads still use the host cache cache/app-sources.
Proxies (crates/vibe-app/src/proxies) and the shell env block are not published to the host for a rootfs target. They are written as target-visible files only.
Refusal error code: `executor-unavailable` (typed AppError variant, exit 1). The message names the step that needs it.
uid/gid: files are owned by the invoking user, and the plan states it. Target-owned metadata waits for the executor capability.
New subcommand name: `vibe app executor check` (read-only). There is no daemon start.
capabilities.risks: Scope creep into the full M-14 target-identity work. Hidden host assumptions in storage/paths (paths.rs, settings.rs) could leak host paths into target files, so a test must check that no absolute host path appears under the root.

capabilities.name: Build, export and replace a container image from a vibe app set
capabilities.user_story: With an executor available, a user runs `vibe app image build apps.vibe-apps --base <base-ref> --tag my/tools:1`. Vibe lowers the rootfs plan into a reviewable build context (`--plan-only` writes it to a directory), runs it through Docker/BuildKit with per-stage progress, and records which packages are in the image. `vibe app image export --oci out.tar` and `vibe app image load` are separate steps. `vibe app image rollback my/tools` re-points the tag to the previous recorded build, and `vibe app image inspect my/tools:1` lists the packages and versions in it. Hooks and service units that need the target run inside the executor, never on the host.
capabilities.todays_form: Consumes the rootfs plan from the capability above. The image build context is derived from that plan, not from display text. The image record reuses the lifecycle build-record shape in crates/vibe-lifecycle/src/mechanism/build/record.rs instead of a new 'closure' ontology. Inspection uses the existing app describe path (crates/vibe-app/src/describe.rs) rather than a new provenance graph in vibe-trace. Offline and mirror supply uses the existing Locator (installer/declared_input.rs) and `--offline`. NOT built: an M-16 operation journal, a generic workflow engine, a store, a Dockerfile compiler beside the plan, or registry push.
capabilities.product_question: After the rootfs-plan slice, should Vibe build OCI images itself (driving docker/buildx), rather than stopping at a rootfs directory the user packages?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Decide after the rootfs slice ships. Building only the build context plus a `docker build` invocation gives most of the value; native BuildKit/LLB is not worth it yet.
prerequisites: Plan apps into a separate root filesystem, refusing when no executor is available
rough_steps: `vibe app image build --plan-only <set> --out <dir>` writes a deterministic build context: a base stage, a payload COPY from the realized rootfs, and executor-run steps for hooks

Executor run: start a disposable container from the base, bind only the rootfs and the cache read-only, run needs-executor steps (hooks, accounts, service units) inside it, and clean up by container id

`vibe app image build` drives `docker buildx build` with that context, streams per-stage progress, and writes an image record (packages, versions, digests, base ref, resulting image id) to app-home images/
`vibe app image export --oci <file>` and `image load` are separate commands; neither pushes
`vibe app image rollback <tag>` re-tags the previous record, and `vibe app image gc` removes records and dangling images not referenced by a tag or a running container
`vibe app image inspect <ref>` reads the record and shows the package list; it falls back to labels inside the image
User doc: a new section in PROP-059 (or a dedicated PROP) written alongside the feature
capabilities.acceptance: On a Linux host with docker: build an image from a vibe-apps/1 set of two archive apps, run `docker run --user 1000 <tag> <cmd> --version` and see that it succeeds. `vibe app image inspect` lists both apps with versions. `image rollback` restores the previous image id. On a host without docker every subcommand except `--plan-only` refuses with `executor-unavailable`.
design_decisions: Command family: `vibe app image {build,export,load,inspect,rollback,gc}` under the existing `vibe app` tree, not a new top-level verb.
Executor: the docker CLI found on PATH (`docker buildx` required for build). It is configured by `[executor] docker = "<path>"` in app settings; there is no auto-install.
Image record location: `<app-home>/images/<tag-sanitized>/<n>.toml`. The newest record is current, and rollback moves a pointer.
Image labels: `org.vibevm.apps=<sha256 of the vibe-apps/1 set>` and `org.vibevm.record=<n>`.
Hook failure inside the executor fails the build and leaves the previous tag untouched. Nothing is undone by deleting files.
Persistent data volumes are out of scope for rollback, and the docs say so.
`--offline` builds must use the host cache and mirrors; the base image must already be present locally.
capabilities.risks: Large Docker-specific surface. Platform variance (Docker Desktop on Windows/macOS). Mixing data rollback with image rollback. Scope pressure to adopt the M-16 journal.

capabilities.name: Install distro packages into a target rootfs through its native package manager
capabilities.user_story: A vibe-apps/1 set may name native distro packages next to vibe apps, for example `native:arch/postgresql`. During `vibe app image build` or a rootfs apply, Vibe runs the distro's own package manager (pacman for an Arch base) inside the executor against the target root. The image record lists the native packages and the repository snapshot used. A failed native hook fails the build visibly and leaves the previous image in place.
capabilities.todays_form: A backend seam in crates/vibe-app/src/installer (beside native.rs and programs.rs, which run upstream installers today), invoked only by needs-executor steps of the rootfs/image plan. The purl type in crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/purl.rs already names foreign packages. NOT built: an abstract transaction port without a real backend, or any touch of the host's package database.
capabilities.product_question: Should Vibe-built environments include distro-native packages (Arch/pacman first), rather than only vibe apps on top of a base image?
capabilities.recommended_answer: No for now. A base image plus vibe apps covers the container use case. Revisit only if the long-term 'Vibe as OS package manager' direction is approved.
prerequisites: Build, export and replace a container image from a vibe app set
rough_steps: Add a `native:<distro>/<name>` item kind to vibe-apps/1, refused unless the target base declares that distro
Run pacman with `--root` inside the executor against the target root, using a pinned repository date/mirror
Record native package names, versions and repo snapshot in the image record
Tests: an update that pulls a new repository epoch, and a hook failure that leaves the previous tag current
capabilities.acceptance: Build an Arch-based image whose set contains `native:arch/jq` and an archive vibe app. `docker run` shows jq and the app both available, and `vibe app image inspect` lists jq with its version and the repo snapshot. A deliberately failing hook leaves the previous image tag current.
design_decisions: The first backend is pacman only. The seam is a trait with one implementation; no in-memory fake ships in the product.
The repository snapshot is pinned by an explicit URL/date in the set, never 'latest' implicitly.
Never run on the host root, refused by a type-level check that the target is a non-host rootfs inside the executor.
capabilities.risks: Large, distro-specific, with an ongoing maintenance burden. Easy to slip into mutating the live system.

capabilities.name: Agents discover and call services running in a Vibe-built environment
capabilities.user_story: After starting a Vibe-built image, `vibe app services list` shows the services the image's packages declare (name, endpoint, MCP or OpenAPI descriptor). An agent connected through vibe's MCP server sees them as tools scoped to that deployment, with probes that report reachable or unreachable. Credentials are never implied by discovery.
capabilities.todays_form: Extends the existing package-to-MCP registration (crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/mcp/package_registration.rs) and app agent configs (crates/vibe-app/src/agents) with endpoints from an image record. It reuses MCP/OpenAPI descriptors and does not duplicate them in a new catalog schema.
capabilities.product_question: Should Vibe register services running in built images as agent tools, rather than leaving that to the agent's own MCP configuration?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Not until images ship and someone runs services in them. Today's MCP registration covers the tools agents need.
prerequisites: Build, export and replace a container image from a vibe app set
rough_steps: Packages declare a `[[service]]` with port and descriptor kind (mcp|openapi); the declaration is copied into the image record
`vibe app services list [--image <ref>]` resolves the endpoints of running containers and probes each one with a timeout
MCP registration exposes reachable mcp-kind services under a deployment-scoped name
Test with two isolated containers: discover both, refuse a stopped one, detect a changed endpoint
capabilities.acceptance: With two containers from Vibe images running, `vibe app services list --json` shows both with status reachable. After one stops, it shows unreachable and its MCP tool is no longer registered.
design_decisions: Descriptor kinds: mcp and openapi only.
Probe timeout 2s, no retries.
Credentials come only from explicit settings, never from discovery.
capabilities.risks: Duplicating MCP config ownership (AGENT-ADAPTER-CONSOLIDATION owns per-agent adapters).

capabilities.name: MCP tools refuse arguments their schema forbids
capabilities.user_story: An agent that calls the `query` tool with `{"limit":"10"}` or `explain` with `{"target":"x","json":"true"}` or any unknown field now gets `isError:true` naming the bad field (e.g. `invalid arguments: limit: invalid type: string "10", expected u64`) instead of a silent run with limit 50 / json=false. Every tool `vibe mcp` serves behaves the same way, and a test sweep proves it for every tool in `default_tools()`.
capabilities.todays_form: Extends crates/vibe-mcp only. Replace ad-hoc `args.get(..).and_then(as_u64/as_bool).unwrap_or(default)` in crates/vibe-mcp/src/tools/query.rs:73-86, select.rs:66-76, explain.rs:56-60 and the three pkgskill/query_package tools in crates/vibe-mcp/src/tools.rs (~178, ~269, ~430-441 incl. `force`) with per-tool `#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` arg structs, the same pattern as tools/lifecycle_run.rs:69 (LifecycleRunArgs) and requirements_query.rs. The original 'universal registry/facade with strict descriptors' (B.1) and 'mechanical coverage matrix' (D.1) are replaced by: strict per-tool decoding plus one unit test iterating default_tools() that sends `{"__unexpected__":true}` (plus required fields) and asserts InvalidArguments. No generic JSON-Schema validator, no dispatcher layer in lib.rs:299-320.
rough_steps: Add a shared helper `fn decode_args<T: DeserializeOwned>(args: &Value) -> Result<T, ToolError>` in crates/vibe-mcp/src/tools.rs that treats Null as `{}` and maps serde errors to ToolError::InvalidArguments(e.to_string())
Convert query, select, explain to typed arg structs; keep limit default 50 and clamp to [1,200] after decode (limit:0 -> InvalidArguments, limit>200 -> clamped, per current descriptor text)
Convert query_package, read_subskill, materialise_subskill (incl. `force: bool` default false) and the zero-arg tools list_tools / agentic_explain (accept `{}`/null, refuse any field)
Add the default_tools() sweep test: unknown field refused for every tool, and a wrong-typed field refused for each tool that has a typed optional field
Update PROP-015 #tools with one sentence: arguments outside the advertised schema are refused, never defaulted
capabilities.acceptance: cargo test -p vibe-mcp passes; new tests: dispatch_one(query {limit:"wrong"}) -> isError:true text contains `limit`; query {unexpected:true} -> isError naming `unexpected`; explain {target:"x",json:"true"} -> isError naming `json`; select {where:"...",limit:5} unchanged result; sweep test covers every name in default_tools() (fails if a new tool omits deny_unknown_fields).
design_decisions: Error channel: Err(ToolError::InvalidArguments(..)) before any build/search runs (preflight; operation did not execute), message = serde error text which names the field
Null or absent `arguments` decodes as an empty object (MCP clients often omit it for zero-arg tools)
limit semantics unchanged: default 50, values >200 clamp to 200 (documented 'clamped'), 0 refused because descriptor says minimum 1

Unknown-field policy uniform for all 16 tools, including configuration_preview/read_doc which already validate via vibe_wire parsers (leave those parsers as is if they already refuse unknown fields; the sweep test verifies)
No change to PROTOCOL_VERSION or descriptor shapes
capabilities.risks: An existing agent prompt or skill_template example that sends extra fields would start failing; grep skill_template.md and PROP-015 examples for extra keys before landing. Do not turn this into a generic schema engine.

capabilities.name: Long lifecycle runs over MCP report progress and can be stopped
capabilities.user_story: An agent calling `lifecycle_run {phase:"build"}` with a `_meta.progressToken` receives `notifications/progress` messages (phase/step counts and a short message) while install and build proceed, instead of a silent multi-minute call. Sending `notifications/cancelled` for that request makes vibe stop cooperatively at the next safe point and return a lifecycle report marked cancelled; `ping` still answers during the run. If a run needs the network while the server was started offline, the refusal says so and how to restart.
capabilities.todays_form: Extends the existing MCP server (crates/vibe-mcp/src/lib.rs dispatch, transport.rs) and lifecycle_run (tools/lifecycle_run.rs, tools/lifecycle_run/ports.rs), reusing the progress seam already threaded into the hosted run (`progress` in ports.rs:148, vibe_core::progress::Progress / vibe_install::InstallProgress) and the existing cooperative token vibe_core::cancellation::CancellationToken (re-exported by vibe-actions/src/invoke.rs:153, used by agent-install stop, tests crates/vibe-cli/tests/cli_agent_stop.rs). Event content mirrors the CLI machine stream (crates/vibe-cli/src/command_progress.rs, PROP-060 #MACHINE-STREAM). Replaces the old 'negotiated framed session with multiplexed queries and replay' and the 'per-operation admission across all adapters' with standard MCP progress/cancel primitives over the existing newline stdio transport. Per-call offline/install override is NOT built: policy stays fixed at server start (deliberate closed `phase` grammar); only its visibility in refusals is added. No daemon, no session replay.
capabilities.product_question: Should `vibe mcp` stream progress and honour client cancellation for lifecycle_run (requires reading stdin on a second thread while a tool runs)?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Yes: lifecycle_run with prerequisite install is the only long MCP call and agents currently block blind with no way to stop it; standard MCP primitives fit without a new protocol.
rough_steps: Split the stdio loop: a reader thread feeds a channel; the dispatcher runs tools/call on the main thread while the reader answers `ping` and records `notifications/cancelled` by requestId

Plumb an MCP progress sink into ServerContext for the duration of one call when `params._meta.progressToken` is present; adapt the hosted run's Progress events into `notifications/progress {progressToken, progress, total?, message}`
Plumb a CancellationToken into the hosted lifecycle run; on cancel return the lifecycle report with its existing interrupted/cancelled outcome (no new wire family)
Ensure offline-blocked refusals in the hosted run name the server-start policy and the restart remedy

Tests in crates/vibe-mcp with MemoryTransport: progress notifications emitted only with a token; cancel mid-run yields cancelled outcome and exactly one provider effect (mirroring cli_agent_stop.rs); ping answered while busy; second tools/call queued, not concurrent
Update PROP-015 #lifecycle and skill_template.md lifecycle_run section
capabilities.acceptance: cargo test -p vibe-mcp: a fixture lifecycle_run with progressToken produces >=1 notifications/progress before the response; with notifications/cancelled sent after the first progress the response is a report whose outcome is cancelled and the fake provider counted exactly one request; without a token no notifications appear (byte-identical to today's output); EOF on stdin during a run requests cancellation and the process exits after the run stops.
design_decisions: Progress only when the client supplies `_meta.progressToken` (MCP spec); never unsolicited

Cancellation is cooperative: 'cancel requested' does not imply stopped; the final response states the actual outcome. Per MCP spec a cancelled request may still return its result; we always return the report
Tool calls stay strictly serial; only ping and notifications are handled concurrently
EOF on stdin while a tool runs = cancellation request, then normal exit
Advertise nothing new in `capabilities` (progress/cancel are base protocol in 2024-11-05); PROTOCOL_VERSION unchanged
No per-call offline/install argument; refusal text: `offline: <what needed network>; this MCP server was started offline — restart `vibe mcp` without --offline`
capabilities.risks: Threading the stdio transport can introduce interleaved writes; all writes must go through one mutex-guarded writer (StdioTransport already uses Mutex). Cancel points must be at existing safe boundaries to avoid half-written state; do not add a second journal.

capabilities.name: Rename a package across the project
capabilities.user_story: A maintainer runs `vibe refactor rename-package org.old/foo org.new/bar --dry-run` and sees every owned reference that will change (its vibe.toml [package] coordinate, dependency entries in other workspace members, spec:// URIs in authored specs) plus zones it will not touch (vibedeps, lock, registries, foreign packages) as warnings. Without --dry-run it rewrites those files preserving formatting, then regenerates derived state via the normal install, and reports the result; `--json` gives the same plan machine-readably.
capabilities.todays_form: A new verb in the existing `vibe refactor` family (crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/refactor/mod.rs, RefactorCommand enum), next to plan-migration / migration-operation / convert-source. Reference census uses existing workspace discovery (as `vibe workspace publish` does, crates/vibe-cli/src/cli/workspace.rs) and manifest model (vibe-core manifest project.rs name/group); edits use toml_edit (already a vibe-core dependency) for manifests and a spec-URI text rewrite for authored spec sources; writes go through vibe-safefs guarded writes as the M-13 migration apply does; regeneration is the ordinary `vibe install` path. The original 'editor buffer barrier', 'pre-effect submission reservation' and 'two-client rename conformance' are dropped: no editor participants exist; tests are ordinary CLI integration tests. Never hand-edits vibedeps or the lockfile.
capabilities.product_question: Does the product want a package rename command (`vibe refactor rename-package`) for packages authored in the current project/workspace?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Yes, scoped to owned authored files in the enclosing workspace: renames are currently a manual multi-file grep across vibe.toml and spec:// URIs, and all building blocks (refactor family, toml_edit, install regeneration) exist.
rough_steps: Census: given old coordinate, discover enclosing workspace, list owned occurrences: [package] name/group of the target, dependency keys/coordinates in member vibe.toml files, spec://<old-group>/<old-name>/ prefixes in authored spec sources under each member's vibevm/vibespecs (excluding vibedeps, .vibe, refs)
Render the plan (human table + --json) with per-file edit counts and a 'not touched' list (lockfile, vibedeps, foreign packages that reference it, published registry copies)
Apply: rewrite files syntax-preservingly (toml_edit; exact-prefix replacement in spec text), all-or-nothing via a pre-flight re-check that each file is unchanged since planning
Optionally move the package directory when --move-dir is given (only for workspace members addressed by path)
Run regeneration through the existing install path unless --no-install; report its outcome
Integration tests in crates/vibe-cli/tests: fixture workspace with two members, dry-run plan JSON, apply, idempotent second run (no-op), refusal when new coordinate already exists
capabilities.acceptance: cargo test -p vibe-cli --test cli_refactor_rename_package: dry-run on a two-member fixture lists exactly the expected files and occurrences and writes nothing; apply leaves `vibe check` green, `vibe tree --json` shows the new coordinate, `grep -r old-coordinate` hits only lockfile history/vibedeps before install and none after; rerun reports no-op; renaming to an existing coordinate exits non-zero with a named conflict.
design_decisions: Command: `vibe refactor rename-package <OLD> <NEW> [--dry-run] [--no-install] [--move-dir <PATH>]`; coordinates in `group/name` form as printed by `vibe tree`
Scope = enclosing workspace members only (owned); foreign references are reported, never edited
Never edit vibedeps/, .vibe/, the lockfile or registries; lock and vibedeps change only via the install run
Spec URI rewrite only on exact `spec://<old-group>/<old-name>/` prefixes in authored sources; anchors/paths untouched
Refuse (exit 2, named error) if NEW already exists in the workspace or a registry index entry is known locally, or if any target file is dirty-changed between plan and apply
JSON envelope `{ok, command:"refactor rename-package", plan:{edits:[{path, occurrences}], untouched:[{path, reason}]}, applied:bool, install:{...}}` following the PROP-036 envelope convention
Version is not changed; published history under the old coordinate is left as is and noted in output
capabilities.risks: Package identity also appears in published registries and other repositories; the command must make clear it only renames locally owned source. Ambiguous short names in dependency tables could cause wrong edits; match full coordinates only.

IDE-TREE-SEARCH will consume the same owner later.

capabilities.name: Inspect retained compile traces without blocking
capabilities.user_story: After `vibe install --trace` or a traced lifecycle run, the user runs `vibe show compile-trace` to list retained runs under `.vibe/trace/` and `vibe show compile-trace <run-id>` (or `--json`) to see its stages, members and which parts are missing, evicted or redacted. capabilities.todays_form: Adds a read-only subcommand to the existing `vibe show` family (crates/vibe-cli/src/cli/inspect.rs ShowSubcommand) over the existing trace store in crates/vibe-workspace/src/compile_trace (store.rs, retention.rs, state.rs). The original 'complete retained debugging structures with exact missing/evicted/redacted state' is expressed as this listing/detail view; no new trace format. Name avoids `vibe trace`, which already delegates to rust-ai-native trace.
capabilities.product_question: Do users need a command to read retained `.vibe/trace/` runs (today they can only be read as files)?
capabilities.recommended_answer: Yes, small: without a reader the --trace flag's output is only usable by reading internal files, and a read-only view is the natural debugging companion; low priority.
rough_steps: Add a read-only open in vibe_workspace::compile_trace that reads the index and run directories without taking TRACE_LOCK, tolerating concurrently written runs (report them as incomplete)
Add `vibe show compile-trace [RUN_ID]` with human table and --json
Tests: listing with zero/one/many runs; detail of an evicted/partial run; succeeds while a test holds the cooperative lock
capabilities.acceptance: cargo test -p vibe-workspace compile_trace read-only tests and cargo test -p vibe-cli show compile-trace test: while the trace lock is held, `vibe show compile-trace --json` exits 0 and lists runs; a run being written is reported with state `incomplete`; no files under .vibe/trace change (checked by hash).
design_decisions: Command `vibe show compile-trace [RUN_ID]`; no RUN_ID lists runs newest first

JSON envelope `{ok, command:"show compile-trace", runs:[{run_id, command, started, state: complete|incomplete|evicted, stages:n}]}`; detail adds `stages:[{name, state, members}]` and `missing`/`redacted` arrays
Never takes the writer lock, never creates or evicts traces
Missing .vibe/trace = empty list, exit 0
capabilities.risks: Reading a run mid-write must never misreport it as complete; derive completeness only from the finalize marker the writer already produces.
